newsitem.title: CHILE: New arrest order issued for Chilean colony doctor.
newsitem.headline: New arrest order issued for Chilean colony doctor.

text.p: A Chilean judge on Monday ordered the arrest of Hartmut Hopp, one of the leaders of a secretive German colony, on charges he covered up child abuse at the enclave and protected its fugitive leader.

Judge Hernan Gonzalez issued the warrant against Hopp, a doctor at the settlement's hospital, as part of an investigation into allegations of child sexual abuse made against Paul Schaefer, who has been on the run from police since last year.
Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, has been accused of sexually molesting at least five Chilean boys at a boarding school run by the colony.

Two weeks ago, Hopp -- widely regarded as Schaefer's No. 2 at Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) -- was arrested to force him to testify before a magistrate investigating whether he and his wife illegally adopted their teenage son, Michael. He was released after the judge questioned him for two hours.
Several hundred Germans live in Bavarian-style houses at the mysterious colony, tucked in the foothills of the Andes 240 miles (300 km) south of Santiago.
Few of the residents speak Spanish, and most have had little contact with the outside world since arriving in Chile over 30 years ago.
Politicians from the ruling centre-left coalition called on the government on Monday to order police to raid the colony again in search of the 76-year-old Schaefer.

"Our patience is exhausted. Chile and its laws are being defied politically and ethically, and we have to find a way of installing a permanent team in the 16,000 hectares (40,000 acres) of Colonia Dignidad to find Schaefer," coalition coordinator Sergio Bitar said.
Repeated police searches of the enclave have failed to find Schaefer, although two men who escaped from it last month said he was holed up in tunnels under forests belonging to the settlement.
One of the men, a 24-year-old German named Tobias Muller, said the colony was being protected by the local police, who warned the settlers when a raid was imminent.
Schaefer, a charismatic Protestant preacher, founded the colony in 1961 after fleeing Germany, where he had been accused of fondling youngsters in an orphanage he set up in Bonn.
